title: Secure Public API Platform
objective: Expose selected resources through a secured, versioned public API.

milestones.title: Milestone 1: OAuth integration and scoped access
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate oauth integration and scoped access in the project.
Document the contract and test one failure or boundary case.

milestones.title: Milestone 2: API usage limits, versioning, and OpenAPI publication
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate api usage limits, versioning, and openapi publication in the project.
Document the contract and test one failure or boundary case.

milestones.title: Milestone 3: Audit logging, security tests, and contract checks
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate audit logging, security tests, and contract checks in the project.
Document the contract and test one failure or boundary case.

milestones.title: Milestone 4: Operational runbook, deprecation policy, and compatibility report
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate operational runbook, deprecation policy, and compatibility report in the project.
Document the contract and test one failure or boundary case.

required_features: API usage limits, versioning, and OpenAPI publication
Audit logging, security tests, and contract checks
Operational runbook, deprecation policy, and compatibility report
stretch_features: Add contract validation to CI and detect a breaking change.
Add structured request IDs and useful metrics without logging secrets.
Document a recovery or migration trade-off with alternatives.
tests: Test success, missing-resource, validation, and authorization outcomes.
Test duplicates and concurrent updates where the domain has non-idempotent side effects.
Run tests against a disposable database with deterministic fixtures.
Review public responses and logs for secret or personal-data exposure.
review_method: Automated tests and static contract checks plus human review against the rubric; no arbitrary learner code executes inside CodeLeaf’s production API.
status_note: Unreviewed project draft; validate scope, starter files, rubric and implementation assumptions before publication.
